title: Packaging & memory
summary: Interposers, HBM stacks and CoWoS: the package is now a system.

links.why: HBM stacks and CoWoS sit inside most big AI chips
advanced packaging is a chokepoint in the chain

ideas.how: HBM sits millimetres from the processor on one interposer
an interposer joins several dies into one system
as shrinking slows, joining and stacking dies carries progress

learn.plain: Packaging used to be just a protective case. Now it is like building a tiny city block: processor buildings next to memory towers, joined by extremely dense roads so data never travels far.
learn.engineer: CoWoS-S uses one silicon interposer; CoWoS-L embeds small silicon bridges in an organic redistribution layer to go beyond the reticle size. Micro-bump pitches are tens of micrometres while hybrid bonding goes below 10 µm. HBM4 doubles the interface to 2,048 bits, and with a foundry-made base die, customers can put custom logic under the memory stack. Heat density, warpage and testing stacks before assembly are the main yield challenges.

options: Stacked DRAM placed beside the processor for very high bandwidth
quiz.why: Rubin carries eight HBM4 stacks for 288 GB of memory.

quiz.q: What does a silicon interposer do?
options: Connects dies side by side with very fine wiring
quiz.why: It provides far more connections than an ordinary package substrate can.

quiz.q: Why do co-packaged optics matter for AI data centers?
options: Light carries data between chips over distance with less power than copper
They remove the need for GPUs
quiz.why: Moving optics into the package cuts the power cost of linking thousands of GPUs.
